cards.explanation: The answer is True. Hezekiah, king of Judah, hears the report and tears his clothes, puts on sackcloth and enters the house of the LORD (Isaiah 37:1). I think he lets how bad it feels show, friends, and then he walks it straight to God's house.

The answer is the house of the LORD. Hezekiah tears his clothes, puts on sackcloth, and enters the house of the LORD (Isaiah 37:1). I bet that news weighs on him, friends, and the text shows him heading straight to God's house.

The answer is Isaiah. Hezekiah sends Eliakim, Shebna and the leading priests to the prophet Isaiah son of Amoz (Isaiah 37:2). They go to a man who speaks for the LORD. Notice the king doesn't go himself, friends. He sends them with a message.

The answer is the living God. Hezekiah says the Rabshakeh was sent by his master the king of Assyria "…to defy the living God…" (Isaiah 37:4). The Rabshakeh's words aren't aimed only at Judah's king, friends. Hezekiah says they're aimed at God Himself.

The answer is False. Hezekiah hopes the LORD will hear the Rabshakeh's words, and he says the LORD "…will rebuke him for the words that the LORD your God has heard." (Isaiah 37:4). He isn't hoping for silence, friends. He's hoping God steps in.

The answer is prayer. Hezekiah ends his message with, "Therefore lift up a prayer for the remnant that still survives." (Isaiah 37:4). He's asking the prophet to pray for the people who are left. When you're out of strength, friends, asking for prayer is a smart move.

The answer is False. The LORD tells Hezekiah, through Isaiah, "Do not be afraid of the words you have heard…" (Isaiah 37:6). I bet after torn clothes and sackcloth, friends, those are good words to hear. The message goes to Isaiah, and the LORD's answer comes back through him.

The answer is that he will return to his own land. The LORD says the king of Assyria will hear a rumor "…and return to his own land…" (Isaiah 37:7). The LORD says He will put a spirit in him, friends. That's His word about where the king is headed.

The answer is that he will fall by the sword. The LORD says that in his own land, "…I will cause him to fall by the sword." (Isaiah 37:7). It's a heavy word, friends, and I think it's meant to be taken seriously. The LORD says what He will do, and the king doesn't get to decide it.

The answer is Libnah. When the Rabshakeh hears that the king of Assyria has left Lachish, he withdraws and finds the king "…fighting against Libnah." (Isaiah 37:8). The king has moved on to a new fight, friends. The Rabshakeh just has to track him down.

The answer is True. Sennacherib, king of Assyria, is warned about Tirhakah king of Cush, who has set out to fight against him. "On hearing this…" Sennacherib sends messengers to Hezekiah (Isaiah 37:9). So even with trouble coming his way, friends, he still sends one more message to Judah.

The answers are God and Jerusalem. Sennacherib says, "Do not let your God, in whom you trust, deceive you…" (Isaiah 37:10). That's his accusation, friends, aimed right at Hezekiah's trust, and Sennacherib is the one saying it, so don't take it as true. He says not to be deceived "…by saying that Jerusalem will not be delivered into the hand of the king of Assyria." (Isaiah 37:10). Jerusalem is the city in the middle of all this, and Sennacherib has his eye on it.

The answer is that your God won't rescue you either. That's Sennacherib's point. He asks, "Will you then be spared?" (Isaiah 37:11). Then he asks, "Did the gods of the nations destroyed by my fathers rescue those nations…?" (Isaiah 37:12). I think he wants Hezekiah to believe Judah is next, friends.

The answer is that he spreads it out before the LORD. Hezekiah receives the letter, reads it, goes up to the house of the LORD and "…spread it out before the LORD." (Isaiah 37:14). He sets the whole thing in front of God, friends. That's a man bringing his problem to the right place.

The answer is False. Hezekiah prays, "…You alone are God over all the kingdoms of the earth." (Isaiah 37:16). He says right to the LORD that He is the only God, friends. Sennacherib's letter had a whole list of gods, and Hezekiah's prayer doesn't.

The answer is Sennacherib. Hezekiah prays, "Listen to all the words that Sennacherib has sent to defy the living God." (Isaiah 37:17). He doesn't hide the letter, friends. He points the LORD right to it.

The answer is that they were only wood and stone. Hezekiah says the Assyrians cast those gods into the fire "…for they were not gods, but only wood and stone…" (Isaiah 37:19). Just a few lines earlier he prays, "…You alone are God over all the kingdoms of the earth." (Isaiah 37:16). He sets those things next to the LORD, friends.

The answer is so all kingdoms know He alone is God. Hezekiah prays, "…save us from his hand, so that all the kingdoms of the earth may know that You alone, O LORD, are God." (Isaiah 37:20). His reason isn't about Judah looking good, friends. He asks that the whole earth would know who God is.
